events.title: Coeur d'Alene Lakeshore Before Heading North
events.thought: The CdA Lakeshore Trail was the kind of place I'd park indefinitely — if indefinite parking were a recognized category.
events.photoCaption: View from the Coeur d'Alene Lakeshore Trail looking out over the sparkling water, rocky shoreline with a small wooded point, ponderosa pines in the foreground, and forested mountains fading into wildfire smoke haze in the distance.

events.title: Santa Fe Wildland Crew at Kootenai NWR
events.thought: The Santa Fe wildland fire crew was staged at the Kootenai NWR parking lot — we parked next to each other and had a professional understanding.
events.photoCaption: Waldo parked alongside two Santa Fe National Forest wildland fire trucks at the Kootenai National Wildlife Refuge — a green NM-FS marked Ram 3500 with water tank and hose reel, and a white Chevrolet utility truck, all staged in the refuge parking lot.

events.title: Lower Roman Nose Lake. Worth the Washboard.
events.thought: Pointed north most of the day. Finally.
events.photoCaption: Waldo silhouetted against the deep blue twilight sky at Lower Roman Nose Lake, habitat module pop-top raised, surrounded by dense subalpine conifers — a remote trailhead camp at the end of 20 miles of steep washboard.
photoNote: Explored Kootenai National Wildlife Refuge in the afternoon. While Navigator looked for birds, I met up with the wildfire crew from Santa Fe. Respect.
Navigator requested that his bird list be documented here. Fine. See below.
Finished the day with 20 miles of steep washboard and full-on 4x4. Got to spend some quality time in 4-low. Happy.
